title: Enterprise intake & priority gating: multi-output hosted API checklist (chat + streaming + toolcalls + structured outputs)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an operationalized intake form, gating rules, prioritization rubric, and onboarding checklist specifically for enterprise Hosted API requests that combine chat, streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs. Goal is to reduce intake friction for Sales/CS, standardize risk signals for Security & SRE, and produce reliable prioritization signals for PM/Eng to decide P0/P1 vs backlog. Includes templates, rollout cadence, and metric contracts for canary enables.
background: Over the past 18 months we have seen a rising class of enterprise requests that are multi-tract: streaming chat sessions that invoke tools or functions at certain steps and return structured JSON for downstream data pipelines. Current intake flows are inconsistent across Sales, Solutions, and CS which creates hidden costs (security reviews missed, infra underprovisioned, SLA mismatches). Several recent incidents highlighted missing gating for customer-provided tool binaries and unclear rollback policies for structured-output regressions.
goals: 1) Define a single intake questionnaire and decision checklist for multi-output feature requests
2) Produce a priority gating rubric that maps signals to required artifacts (security review, infra sizing, legal/contract clauses)
3) Ship an onboarding checklist that enables a 2-week readiness window for canarying with dedicated capacity
4) Codify metrics and dashboards to validate cost/quality tradeoffs during rollout
acceptance_criteria: Intake form (Sales/CS/Partner-facing) published in Confluence with examples and minimum required attachments
Gating rubric documented: required if any of (customer-managed tool integration, PII data flow, >1TB/month token estimate, cross-region routing)
Priority classifier (automated rule set) implemented in intake tracker prototype: outputs candidate priority + required approvals
Onboarding checklist in Console runbook with steps for: test harness, golden prompt set, structured-output schema validation, canary config
Dashboard (Console) tiles for: per-tenant token estimate, latency SLO risk, structured-output schema validation failures, toolcall error rates
proposed_solution: Deliver a 3-part artifact: (A) a one-page intake questionnaire and attachment template for Sales/CS; (B) a decision rubric that maps risk signals to 'must-have' reviews (security, infra, legal) and a numerical priority score; (C) an onboarding runbook for eng + solutions to execute a canary. Implement a prototype of the rule-based priority classifier as a spreadsheet and integrate into the intake tracker (low-effort automation). Work with Security to create a fast-track review checklist for low-risk toolcalls.
tradeoffs: Stricter gating reduces runway time-to-market but increases friction for customers and load on Solutions. Lightweight rule automation may misclassify nuanced requests — mitigate by adding mandatory human-in-loop for any 'borderline' score. Investing in schema validation for structured outputs increases initial engineering cost but reduces downstream consumer failures. Full automation of approvals would be ideal long-term but requires additional guardrails (audit logs/KMS) which push this into Q3.
notes: Link: initial PRD draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Enterprise+Multi-Output+Intake+PRD
implementation_steps: 1. Workshop with Solutions, Sales, Security, SRE (3/12) to validate signals and examples
2. Author intake questionnaire and two canonical examples (chat+streaming+toolcall, chat->structured-output) (owner: PM)
3. Build priority rubric spreadsheet and simulation using last 50 enterprise requests to calibrate thresholds (owner: PM + Data)
4. Prototype rule output integration into intake tracker (low-code automation) (owner: Eng)
5. Create Console runbook + onboarding checklist and mock dashboards (owner: DevEx)
6. Pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers over 2 weeks, run canaries with dedicated capacity, capture metrics
7. Iterate and finalize playbook, publish Confluence + notify Sales/CS
metrics_and_signals: Per-request token estimate vs provisioned dedicated capacity (tokens/day)
Canary quality: structured-output schema pass rate (percent) over 1000 examples
Toolcall reliability: error rate per 1k calls
Latency SLO breach probability during burst windows
risk_mitigation: Require human-in-loop for any automated classifier score in 40-60 range
Add mandatory schema contract and validator for any structured output used in downstream integrations
Security: block customer-managed executable uploads until Security signoff; allow webhook-driven toolcalls via vetted proxy
Budget protection: initial canary on Dedicated with strict quota and auto-fallback to hosted generic model if errors exceed threshold
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish intake form + rubric, internal training for Sales & Solutions
Week 1: Pilot with 3 strategic accounts, collect metrics and feedback
Week 2: Iterate on onboarding checklist and automate top 3 gating checks
Week 3-4: Expand to all enterprise intake channels, enable automated priority hints in tracker
Post-launch: monthly review with Security, SRE, and Solutions to adjust thresholds
